text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Three Israeli soldiers were killed and one seriously wounded when a roadside bomb exploded near their patrol in south Lebanon.
-Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu called on Syria to stop Hizbollah guerrilla attacks on Israeli forces in Lebanon.
-Opposition MPs will take the floor on the third day of the 1997 state budget debate.
-Tunisian airlines will resume flights to Lebanon in June.
-Teachers at the state-run Lebanese University to stage a one-day strike on Friday to protest against the government's financial policy towards the university.
-Prime Minister Hariri said his government was ready to open a dialogue with the General Labour Confederation on social issues.
-Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest said it will increase its capital by $13.75 million to $40 million through a private share placement.
-In its annual human rights report, the United States accused the Lebanese government of curbing freedoms.
-Diplomatic relations between Lebanon and Jordan have deteriorated. The charge d'affaires is handling the Jordanian embassy in Beirut in the absence of the ambassador.
